cases.text: The lighthouse keeper had kept a logbook for thirty-one years, and in all that time he had never missed an entry. Most days the entries were short: the direction of the wind, the height of the swell, the ships that passed and the hour they passed. On the morning the supply boat failed to arrive, he wrote the same things he always wrote, and then, after a long pause, he added a line he had never written before. He wrote that he was not sure whether anyone would read the book again. Then he closed it, wound the clockwork that turned the lamp, and went down the spiral stairs to check the oil, because whatever happened to the boat, the light would still need to burn that night.

cases.text: Worked example. A tank holds 1,250 litres and drains at 3.75 litres per minute. After 47 minutes it has lost 47 x 3.75 = 176.25 litres, leaving 1,250 - 176.25 = 1,073.75 litres. At that rate it empties after 1,250 / 3.75 = 333.33 minutes, about 5 hours 33 minutes. Check: 333 x 3.75 = 1,248.75 and 334 x 3.75 = 1,252.50. The first 30 digits of pi are 3.14159265358979323846264338327, and 2^20 = 1048576.
